usage: decode_fixed.py [-h] [--tokens TOKENS] [--jsonl JSONL] port [alias]

Fixed-output online decode screening, using final usage token counts. Usage:
decode_fixed.py <port> [alias] [--tokens 128] [--jsonl PATH] Every prompt gets
one discarded warmup and three formal samples. A sample must finish at its
requested token limit, with final usage and [DONE]. HTTP exposes visible text
arrivals, not exact generated-token timing; native decode is the authority for
formal performance acceptance.

positional arguments:
  port
  alias

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --tokens TOKENS
  --jsonl JSONL    append complete timing/usage records (including warmups and
                   rejections)

usage: prefill_decode_bench.py [-h] [--decode-tokens DECODE_TOKENS]
                               [--jsonl JSONL]
                               port [ctx_sizes ...]

Online TTFT and decode screening, using final usage token counts. Usage:
prefill_decode_bench.py <port> [ctx_sizes...] [--decode-tokens 512] [--jsonl
PATH] Prefill requests use max_tokens=1 and a random leading nonce.
tokens/TTFT is an end-to-end estimate including cache/restore, first-token
work and HTTP transport. usage.prompt_tokens alone cannot prove a cache miss:
inspect server evidence. Decode timing from visible text cannot replace native
generated-token timing.

positional arguments:
  port
  ctx_sizes

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --decode-tokens DECODE_TOKENS
  --jsonl JSONL         append complete timing/usage records (including
                        warmups and rejections)
